name: Weighted Neck Flexion
summary: An isolation exercise that strengthens the anterior cervical spine flexors by raising the head against added resistance while lying supine.

setup: Lie supine on a flat bench with your shoulders near the edge so your head and upper neck hang off freely.
Place a folded towel or small pad over your forehead for comfort.
Position a light weight plate on top of the towel over your forehead, holding it lightly with both hands to keep it stable.
steps: Slowly lower your head backward into comfortable cervical extension.
Flex your neck to raise your head, drawing your chin smoothly toward your chest.
Pause briefly at peak flexion, then lower under control back to the starting stretch.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower your head and exhale smoothly as you flex your neck upward.
cues: Tuck the chin as you curl up
Keep hands only as guides on the plate

common_faults.fault: Using your hands to push or lift the plate
common_faults.correction: Hold the plate only to balance it; let the neck muscles produce all the lifting force.

common_faults.fault: Jerking or moving too quickly through cervical extension
common_faults.correction: Perform all repetitions with a deliberate, controlled tempo to protect the cervical spine.

precautions: Start with very light resistance or bodyweight only to assess neck tolerance before adding weight.
Stop immediately if you experience sharp pain, dizziness, or radiating symptoms.
